questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Texas due to the high ranked law school, nice city, good weather and close to family and friends in the US.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy find information, but it did require a lot of work to apply, fill out various forms, find accomodation and just plan the exchange in general.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mauricio from University of Texas provided a lot of assistance and definitely helped me a lot with finding information and making sure everything was completed correctly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was rather hard to find affordable accomodation in Austin close to campus. I lived at one of the Co-ops which was cheaper than other places and had more availability, but the Co-op I lived at (Taos) was very worn down and it took some time getting used to living there. The Halstead or Laurel co-op are more recommendable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I recommend living in West Campus in Austin, it is close to campus and it is the "real" college experience. It is rather expensive to live in West Campus though (DKK 6.000 - 12.000) depending on where you chose to live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to fill out some online forms and write a motivational letter. It was rather easy and UT provided a lot of support.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mauricio provided a lot of assistance and was easy to get in touch with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Exchange students were prioritized lower than American and LL.M. students, so I did not get any of my top 5 priorities in registering for classes. I ended up being really happy with my classes though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend keeping an open mind and taking some classes which are not offered at your home university. Also, try some classes which are taught differently from KU (E.g. Energy Development and Policy).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It took some time getting used to the way the classes were taught (cold calling and a lot more class participation compared to KU).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses at the law school and I think the level varied of the courses a lot. Some of the classes were hard (Constitutional law and Energy Development and Policy), while other classes were easier (Wall Street Regulation and Legal Research).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching varied a little with more class preparation during the semester and cold calling, but it was fun to experience a different teaching style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Constitutional law for foreign lawyers (Mandatory)
- Contracts for foreign lawyers
- Energy Development and Policy
- Wall Street Regulation
- Advanced legal research: Corporations & Securities

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Wall street regulation was a fun course if you are interested in Wall Street and investments/stocks/businesses in general.

Energy development and policy was also a fun course, however, hard. It was taught as a project throughout the semester where law students, MBA students and engineering students had to collaborate to make a energy portfolio that could be pitched to an investor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Insurance and housing was rather expensive and I spent a lot of money on travelling as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing was more expensive than I expected. The cost of living is rather high, but definitely worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Make sure to go the university sport's events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The football games were a lot of fun, but sport in general was very important to the local students and it was a good way to become part of the school culture.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Football games (any sport in general), Austin City Limits (festival), travel around the US.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely go SUP-boarding on Lady Bird Lake in downtown Austin in the summer and fall.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: COVID-19 affected our opportunities to socialize a lot and a lot of social activities through the university were cancelled. I recommend participating in some of the events for international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food culture took some time getting used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming and friendly Americans.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. University of Texas at Austin is an amazing place to study, the university is good and the city is really awesome as well. 

2. Apply for scholarships, an exchange year is expensive, but definitely worth it!

3. Be prepared to spend quite a bit of time to apply and plan the exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do an exchange! It's a really rewarding experience that will help grow both personally and academically.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends and encounter with different cultures. It helps you to learn a lot about a different culture and yourself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Due to COVID-19, there was a lot of uncertainty in the beginning which was a stressful and challenging time, but it was all worth it in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: All the hard work prior to the exchange is worth it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
